name: Recording yourself

lead: Recording yourself means capturing your speech on a phone or microphone and listening back to get feedback on how you sound. In voice-improvement discussions it is treated as a basic feedback step.
No studies were found testing it for changing perceived attractiveness or authority.

paras: Playback lets a speaker hear pacing, filler words and tone from outside, which practitioners say differs from how one hears oneself while talking.
No risks are documented in the sources reviewed.

studies.title: Understanding youths' attitudes and practices regarding listening to music, video recording and terrain park use while skiing and snowboarding.

lead: Recording yourself is the practice of capturing one's speech or voice and listening back to review it. In voice-improvement communities it is described as a feedback tool used alongside exercises such as reading aloud or slowing one's pace.
No studies were found that test self-recording as a voice or appearance intervention, so this entry is brief.
